matches.upshot_note: BETBOOM at 37.2% is a real shot at an upset, and the format helps them: a Bo5 gives them five maps, their only loss in this event was 0-2 to FURIA in the group stage, and they have already beaten Falcons 2-1 in a semi-final. But the ratings model still has FURIA 233 points ahead (1829 v 1596), FURIA are the higher-ranked side (#4 v #14) and in form (4/5, straight sets against Aurora in the semi-final), and there is no HotSpawn crowd split or book price for this match to fade. So the pick is FURIA and BETBOOM is published as the upset shot at 37.2% rather than taken.

day5_context.statement: What days 1-4 actually say about the two day-5 matches.

points.text: Two favourites have already been beaten in this event: 9z over Aurora on day 1 and BETBOOM over Falcons on day 4. The market has been wrong twice in the same direction.

Both upsets were price-driven, not form-driven: 9z were roughly 3.80 with Thunderpick and Falcons roughly 73% across three books. In both cases the underdog was a low-ranked side, and in both cases the underdog's own upset was the outlier rather than a trend.
FURIA have won both meetings with BETBOOM in this event, 2-0 on 14 October in the group stage, and are 4-1 in their last five series.

sources.label: HLTV grand-final odds page (head-to-head, FURIA 2-0 BETBOOM on 14 Oct)

points.text: Rest: FURIA's last match was the 14:00Z semi-final on 17 October; BETBOOM's was the 17:00Z semi-final on the same day. Both played on 17 October and both rest 17 hours before the final. There is no rest edge on either side.

Map-pool edge: on HLTV's own numbers over the last six months, FURIA's Inferno win rate is 71% across 14 maps and their Anubis win rate is 0% across 4. BETBOOM's Dust2 win rate is 64% across 14 maps and their Nuke win rate is 59% across 17. Both vetoes have a way to hurt the favourite, which is exactly what a Bo5 punishes.

points.text: The two day-5 matches are a Bo3 for third place and a Bo5 for the title. A Bo5 gives the underdog more maps to win, which is the one structural reason to look at BETBOOM at all — but it is not a reason to take them below our own 35% floor.

flags.title: The bo3.gg 'rating' field is a tournament-level metric and is not used as a win probability
flags.detail: Every match of the same bo3.gg tournament carries the same 'rating' value (for example 0.0416 for the whole of tournament 6050), so it cannot be a per-match win probability. Only bo3.gg's bookmaker coefficients inside 'bet_updates' are used, and only when both sides carry one. This is recorded because the field is easy to mistake for a model probability.

flags.title: HotSpawn's own crowd percentages are never a probability input
flags.detail: HotSpawn's 'picked %' is carried on every row as leaderboard context only, labelled as such, and is excluded from every probability. The published probability comes from external bookmaker prices, or from the official Valve ratings model when no book prices the match.

flags.title: Valve's official ratings snapshot used is 2026-10-05
flags.detail: Valve's counter-strike_regional_standings repository publishes a dated global standings file; the newest one in the repository is live/2026/standings_global_2026_10_05.md. Ratings are therefore twelve days old at the time of this page, inside the fourteen-day freshness rule the canonical board already applies, but they are not a live feed.
